data.q: Which namespace contains the primary types for file I/O operations in .NET?
data.e: System.IO contains classes like File, Directory, FileStream, StreamReader, and StreamWriter for file and stream operations.

data.q: What is the recommended way to read all text from a file asynchronously in modern .NET?
data.e: File.ReadAllTextAsync returns a Task<string> and must be awaited. It was added in .NET Core 2.1 / .NET Standard 2.1.

data.q: Which class provides a forward-only reader for UTF-8 encoded text files with high performance?
data.e: StreamReader is the standard text reader. Utf8JsonReader is for JSON token parsing, not general text file reading.

data.q: When using FileStream, which FileMode creates a new file or overwrites an existing file?
data.e: FileMode.Create creates a new file or truncates an existing file. CreateNew throws if the file exists. OpenOrCreate opens existing or creates new without truncating.

data.q: Which serialization library is the built-in default for JSON in .NET Core 3.0+ and .NET 5+?
data.e: System.Text.Json is the high-performance, built-in JSON serializer. Newtonsoft.Json (Json.NET) is a popular third-party alternative.

data.q: How do you configure System.Text.Json to write indented (pretty-printed) JSON?
data.e: The property is WriteIndented (not Indented). Pass the options instance to JsonSerializer.Serialize.

data.q: Which attribute marks a property to be ignored during System.Text.Json serialization?
data.e: [JsonIgnore] is the System.Text.Json attribute. [IgnoreDataMember] is for DataContractSerializer. [NonSerialized] is for BinaryFormatter.

data.q: What is the correct way to serialize an object to a JSON file asynchronously?
o: await using var stream = File.Create(path); await JsonSerializer.SerializeAsync(stream, obj);
data.e: SerializeAsync writes directly to a stream asynchronously. It avoids allocating the full JSON string in memory. The stream should be disposed via await using.

data.q: Which class is used for binary serialization in .NET (legacy, not recommended for new development)?
data.e: BinaryFormatter (in System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters.Binary) is obsolete and insecure. BinaryWriter writes primitives, not object graphs.

data.q: How do you get the directory portion of a file path in a platform-agnostic way?
data.e: All three approaches work. Path.GetDirectoryName is the most direct. FileInfo and DirectoryInfo provide additional file system metadata.

data.q: Which method creates a directory recursively (including parent directories) if it doesn't exist?
data.e: Directory.CreateDirectory creates all directories in the path. It returns a DirectoryInfo and does not throw if the directory already exists.

data.q: What is the purpose of FileOptions.Asynchronous when opening a FileStream?
o: Enables async I/O at the OS level for better scalability
Makes all operations on the stream asynchronous automatically
Allows the file to be opened by multiple processes simultaneously
Forces the file to be opened in read-only mode
data.e: FileOptions.Asynchronous (or FileShare.ReadWrite with async) enables overlapped I/O on Windows, improving scalability for high-concurrency async file operations.

data.q: Which interface should a class implement to support custom serialization with System.Text.Json?
data.e: System.Text.Json does not use interface-based serialization callbacks. Custom serialization is done via JsonConverter<T> registered in JsonSerializerOptions.

data.q: How do you handle circular references when serializing object graphs with System.Text.Json?
data.e: ReferenceHandler.Preserve (added in .NET 6) emits $id/$ref metadata to preserve object identity and handle cycles. IgnoreCycles is another option to simply skip cycles.

data.q: What is the difference between File.Copy and File.Move when the destination file already exists?
o: Copy throws; Move overwrites by default
Copy overwrites by default; Move throws
data.e: Both File.Copy and File.Move throw IOException if the destination exists. Use the overload with overwrite: true to replace.

data.q: Which method reads a file line by line with minimal memory allocation using a struct enumerator?
data.e: File.ReadLines returns IEnumerable<string> that streams lines lazily. ReadAllLines loads all lines into a string[] array. The struct enumerator (since .NET Core 2.1) avoids allocations.
